name: berkeley-db
why: An old embedded key/value database with a long history; a strange old-school engine worth exploring for its internals.

brief.what_it_is: Berkeley DB is a family of embedded key/value database libraries, according to Oracle's homepage. Applications link the library and reach data through simple function-call APIs, with listed bindings for C, C++, Java/JNI, C#, Python and Perl. The homepage lists BTREE, HASH, QUEUE and RECNO storage methods, an SQL API made by incorporating SQLite, and a Java Direct Persistence Layer and Collections API. The Homebrew package installs 15 companion utilities (db_dump, db_load, db_verify, db_recover, db_stat and others), but the homepage does not describe them, so their roles are unverified beyond their names.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as a way to build custom data management without the overhead traditionally associated with custom projects, using well-proven building blocks that can be configured for needs 'from the hand-held device to the data center'.
brief.how_it_works: The homepage says the products use function-call APIs for data access and management, and offer selectable storage access methods (BTREE, HASH, QUEUE, RECNO). It also lists replication for high availability as a feature. It does not explain the internals (log, locking, page cache) in the pages I read.
brief.install_notes: Nothing install-specific appeared on the homepage. The docs page I reached is for Berkeley DB XML 6.0.18 (2015), not the core library, and it points to separate Unix and Windows build guides that I did not fetch. No account or runtime is required by anything I saw; the Oracle sign-in and cloud links on the page are unrelated navigation.
brief.standout: It is a library, not a server: you link it into your program and call it directly, with no network hop. The family also spans three implementations (C, Java Edition, XML) and a SQLite-backed SQL front end, which is an unusual range for a single old embedded engine.
brief.status: quiet, inferred and not confirmed. The newest release the homepage announces is Version 18.1 from June 14, 2018. The docs page I fetched is for XML 6.0.18 from July 2015. I did not check a commit history or release feed, so treat this as a guess from page dates.
brief.caveats: The homepage is Oracle marketing copy, so it gives no commands, install steps or limits. The docs I fetched belong to a different (XML) product from 2015, so they do not describe the core tools. Licensing was not verified from the pages I read. The scout note's 'strange old-school engine' is an impression, not something the pages state.
quotes: Berkeley DB is a family of embedded key-value database libraries providing scalable high-performance data management services to applications.
The Berkeley DB products use simple function-call APIs for data access and management.
from the hand-held device to the data center, from a local storage solution to a world-wide distributed one, from kilobytes to petabytes.
